subject: Post-call: e2e response-time targets & next steps (p95/p99) - Veridian Health
messages:
From: Jared Liu <jared.liu@veridian.health>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Jan 2027 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery — latency/throughput constraints (Veridian)

Hi Rachel / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good conversation. To confirm the performance constraints we discussed on the call and to make sure the upcoming PoC focuses on the right metrics:

- Workload: real-time clinical triage assistant (short prompts, typical response lengths ~80-200 tokens).
- Expected sustained throughput: ~500–650 qps during peak windows.
- Concurrency: target ~60 parallel user sessions at peak (workload is bursty).
- E2E latency targets (from user request to final token delivered): p95 <= 220 ms, p99 <= 480 ms.
- Streaming: client expects low first-byte latency for streaming responses (first chunk <= 120 ms) and steady incremental updates — jitter matters.
- SLA sensitivity: p99 regressions > 20% will trigger an ops escalation.

We can share anonymized traces and a small traffic dump if that helps with environment matching. For the PoC we want to compare Redwood Hosted against our incumbent provider under a controlled replay.

Next steps from our side: I can send a sample traffic replay (5k requests) and a schema for acceptable measurement. When can your team ingest a replay and run a baseline?

-Jared

--
Jared Liu
Platform Engineering, Veridian Health
ops@veridian.health

Hi Jared — great summary, thank you.

Couple of clarifying items so our PoC matches your acceptance criteria exactly:
1) For throughput: is 500–650 qps sustained or peak burst? (you mentioned "peak windows")
2) For concurrency: is 60 sessions the max simultaneous open sessions, or the number of concurrent active token-generating streams?
3) For streaming first-byte SLAs, is the 120 ms requirement for the very first chunk only, or must each incremental chunk also be <=120 ms under steady state?

Plan on our side: Ben (cc'd) will schedule a replay ingestion slot and Monica will own the test plan + measurement framework. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail distribution, and streaming first-byte histograms.

Proposed timing: ingestion + smoke by Tue 1/12, two PoC runs Wed 1/13, analysis Thu 1/14. Does that align with your schedule?

Thanks — Rachel

- Define the exact metrics and measurement hooks (timestamps at client send, server receive, first-byte, final-byte).

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 07:02:00 -08:00
Subject: PoC test plan + measurement methodology (draft)

Rachel / Ben — attached is a first draft of the PoC test plan (redwood-poc-test-plan.pdf). Key highlights:

- Measurement hooks: client send timestamp (t0), server receive (t1), first-byte delivered (t2), final-byte delivered (t3). We will compute e2e latency as t3 - t0 for final-token, and first-byte latency as t2 - t0.
- Aggregation: 1s sliding windows for p95/p99, with 1-minute reporting buckets to avoid noisy spikes.
- Load profile: baseline sustained 300 qps for 10m, 3 burst windows (650 qps) of 60s spaced across run, and a long tail 10m ramp to 500 qps. Concurrency emulator will open N sessions and keep them active to match "60 concurrent sessions" behavior.
- Streaming: we will replay streaming traces to verify first-byte under partial tokens; we will capture chunk inter-arrival times.
- Environment: Redwood Hosted pinned in us-west-2, model variant: rwd-qual-1 (8-bit QAT), concurrency setting capped at 64.
- Success criteria: p95 <= 220 ms AND p99 <= 480 ms across three consecutive runs; first-byte median <= 120 ms and 95th <= 220 ms.

Open questions for Jared (to confirm with Veridian):
1) Are there any third-party intermediaries (CDN, web socket gateways) in front of the model that we should reproduce?
2) Can we use a synthetic client that reproduces your auth headers, or do we need to use your staging tokens?

Please review; I can send this to Jared once we confirm the two questions above.

Attachments: redwood-poc-test-plan.pdf (draft)

Thanks,
Monica

--
Monica Patel
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
